chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafī said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

about this matter, so he said, 'Repeat it to me.' I said to him, 'I had a slave-girl who did not bear me a child, so I sold her. She bore a child by another man, and I had a child by another woman. Should I marry my son to her daughter?' He said, 'Marry the child she had before you [to your son], meaning before that [child] was born.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a son to the daughter of a slave-girl he sold, if she bore the child by another man?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Al-Husn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafī inquires of Imam al-Rida (AS) regarding the marriageability of a son to the daughter of a slave-girl he previously owned, who bore a child by another man during his ownership. The Imam clarifies that the child is considered his offspring for the purpose of marriage, emphasizing that the status is determined by the time of birth while she was still in his possession. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that paternity in the context of *mukatab* or owned slaves is established by the master's ownership at the time of the child's birth, facilitating valid intra-family marriages.
